On Mon, Jan 23, 2023 at 10:18 AM Garth Willis <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Michael,
I am finally able to circle back to you on this now that we have a version of the Atrocity Prevention /
Tech company engagement framework that while not final, is ready to be shared.
After many conversations with State and the NSC we were able to pare down the NSC vision to have a
much longer list of countries for the pilot phase to 2-4 countries. In discussions with State it was
mutually agreed that two countries that would work well for the pilot phase are Burma and Bangladesh.
This of course is contingent on Regional Bureau/Mission concurrence.
Would you be able to share this with your team? We would be open for a further discussion with any
questions you may have. Also as an FYI NSC is hoping that we can have a workshop with tech
companies in the coming weeks/months where we will discuss the framework broadly, this workshop
will be led by State with support from USAID.
Short term asks would be to get concurrence that Burma and Bangladesh are appropriate for inclusion,
that there is Bureau/Mission buy-in, and a POC for engagement moving forward. As you mentioned
earlier, this can be seen as a good opportunity to get the attention of Tech companies that are active in
the two countries, and to use the inter-agency to bring our perspectives to their approach to monitoring
and responding to events on the ground.
Garth
